keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1228-1511, the whole life before the first loss. FIX of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a): the first draft was an unclipped 170 km disc round Dibrugarh (347 cells, about 87,000 km2) that contained the whole ahom-kingdom 1228 shape and ran 45 cells into Myanmar and 30 into Nagaland. Frame now from the page (re-read 2026-11-01): 'bound by the Himalayas on the north, river Burhi Dihing on the south, Patkai ranges on the east'; Dutta's western limit the Bharali, others 'the Viswanath area'; core 'almost the entire region of present districts of Lakhimpur, Dhemaji, Tinsukia, and parts of Dibrugarh'; Nath: at its zenith the authority 'extended only marginally into the surrounding hills'. Drawn as Assam within 110 km of Sadiya or 60 km of {93.6E 27.1N} (north bank, Itanagar side) plus Arunachal within 75 km of Sadiya or 45 km of Itanagar (117 cells, about 29,600 km2), clipped to Assam and Arunachal Pradesh so nothing reaches Myanmar or Nagaland, MINUS the ahom-kingdom 1228 land (Assam inside 90 km of Dibrugarh, 53 cells) but with the Sadiya 30 km disc kept (the capital). Result 87 cells, about 22,011 km2 (26 in Assam, 61 in Arunachal); the page gives no area, and the Ahom kingdom's infobox 41,958 km2 (1826) is the nearest check, ratio about 0.5. DISAGREEMENT: the Ahom disc round Dibrugarh (27.48N) also covers Dhemaji, Tinsukia and North Lakhimpur, which the page names as the Chutia core, while the Ahom dossier's own text puts the Ahom core at Charaideo (27.03N) and the Ahom page (re-read 2026-11-01) has the main body 'finally settled by 1253 in the fertile Dikhou valley', now Sibsagar district; subtracting it leaves only 26 Assam cells to the Chutias, so this shape is too small in Assam until ahom-kingdom re-centres its 1228 shape on Charaideo/Sivasagar (then drop the subtrahend and the Chutia frame returns about 30 more cells). Five cells of the Sadiya disc still overlap the Ahom disc and go away with that re-centring.

FIX of 2026-11-01: the first draft subtracted the Ahom Habung disc (Assam inside 110 km of Dibrugarh) whole, which took Sadiya (82 km from Dibrugarh) out of the Chutia shape although the pages have the Chutias holding it until the fall ('The Chutias fortified Sadiya, but they were soon defeated'; 'Sadiakhowa Gohain looked after the Sadia region taken from the Chutias in 1524'). The Sadiya 30 km disc is now kept. Habung: the Chutia and Suhungmung pages say only 'with headquarters at Habung (located in present-day Lakhimpur)' and 'Panbari of Habung'; the Lakhimpur district page (opened 2026-11-01) does not mention it, so Habung is still not placed and the Ahom dossier's 110 km disc is mirrored (it should be re-centred on Lakhimpur). ledger.note: 1228: the Chutia state stands round Sadiya as the Ahoms arrive. 'The Chutias established a state in the plains around Sadiya before the advent of the Ahoms in 1228'; the page also says it was 'believed to be founded in the early 13th century around Sadiya and contiguous areas', the infobox has 'Established: Unknown (before Ahom state)', and Nath holds that 'the evidence is scarce that it was of any significance before the second half of the 14th century'. The page gives no founding year, so 1228 is a bridge at confidence 1 (re-read 2026-11-01); the kamarupa-kingdom dossier hands this land over in 1140, so 1140-1228 is unmapped. The region no longer includes the Ahom 1228 land (Assam inside 90 km of Dibrugarh) except Sadiya.

ledger.note: 1512: Suhungmung annexes Habung. 'He annexed Habung, a Chutia dependency in 1512'; the Chutia page: 'annexed Panbari of Habung in 1512, which, according to Amalendu Guha, was a Chutia dependency'. Mirror of ahom-kingdom ledger 2, whose region is used here without the Sadiya 30 km disc (Sadiya is 82 km from Dibrugarh and was still the Chutia capital in 1523). The pages place Habung only 'in present-day Lakhimpur' (Lakhimpur district page: silent).

region.text: the Chutia kingdom and its border with the Ahoms (the Ahom dossier's region)

ledger.note: 1513: the Ahom-Chutia war begins. 'The Chutia king Dhirnarayan attacked the Ahoms at Dikhoumukh the next year, but was unsuccessful' (Suhungmung page); the Chutia page: 'In 1513 a border conflict triggered the Chutia king Dhirnarayan' to advance to Dikhowmukh. The Chutias also attacked 'in 1520 and occupied the areas up to Namdang and Mungkhrang', and the Ahoms re-occupied them in 1522 (Suhungmung page); those swings are not drawn. Mirror of ahom-kingdom ledger 3. NOT DRAWN (review g-sa-a, 2026-11-01): the Suhungmung page says 'The Chutias again attacked the Ahoms in 1520 and occupied the areas up to Namdang and Mungkhrang' and 'In 1522, the Ahoms fought back, re-occupied their lost territories'; no occupation_start/occupation_end pair is written because no page places Namdang ('Nam Deng, red river', a frontier) and the Chutia page puts Mungkhrang only 'at the mouth of the Dihing river', the Ahom dossier has no 1520 or 1522 event to mirror, and the land lies in the Ahom core that keyframe 0 subtracts. The 1513-1523 contest zone covers it.

1523: the war ends with the Chutia kingdom annexed. 'In 1522, the Ahoms fought back, re-occupied their lost territories and invaded the Chutia kingdom' by 'erecting a fort at the mouth of Dibru/Tiphao (Dibrugarh)', then marched on Sadiya, where 'the Chutias fortified Sadiya, but they were soon defeated'. Mirror of ahom-kingdom ledger 4.

notes: No Cliopatria row. REPAIR of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a, verdict fail): (1) the 1228-1511 shape was an unclipped Dibrugarh 170 km disc (347 cells) that contained the whole Ahom 1228 shape and ran into Myanmar and Nagaland; it is now the page's frame (Assam and Arunachal only, 117 cells before subtraction) minus the ahom-kingdom 1228 land, leaving 87 cells (about 22,000 km2; page gives no area, Ahom infobox 41,958 km2 for 1826). (2) Sadiya, the capital, was outside the 1512-1522 shape; the Sadiya 30 km disc is now kept out of the Ahom land in 1228-1522. (3) The 1520-1522 Chutia occupation up to Namdang and Mungkhrang is not drawn (see ledger 2). OPEN FOR ahom-kingdom (not edited here): its 1228 shape (Assam inside 90 km of Dibrugarh) and its 1512 Habung disc contain Sadiya and the Chutia core (Dhemaji, Tinsukia, North Lakhimpur); re-centre the 1228 shape on Charaideo (94.87E 27.03N) and Habung on Lakhimpur, then drop the Ahom subtrahend from keyframes 0-1 here. START: the page gives no founding year; 1228 is a bridge at confidence 1; kamarupa-kingdom lists this state as a successor at 1140, so 1140-1228 is unmapped. END: 1523 (Ahom, infobox '1523-24'); the Suhungmung page has the Sadia region 'taken from the Chutias in 1524' and an officers' list on the Ahom page says 1524. RULERS: the Chutia page lists Nandi to Dhirnarayana with dated inscriptions (1392, 1401, 1428, 1442) but no reign years, so no ruler strip. NOT TOUCHED: the Chutia refuges in Arunachal after 1523 (Chandangiri, Doithang) and the Chutia descendants' settlement at Bihbari (undated); Koch-Kamata contacts. Gazetteer names needed: Sadiya (place, 27.83N 95.65E; regions here use the coordinate), Habung (location unknown, 'present-day Lakhimpur').
